name: Cedric Bellamy
source_profile:
Marquis Cedric Bellamy “the Tollkeeper” 
A wealthy southern aristocrat whose family's fortunes were 
made in trade rather than warfare. Bellamy possesses a 
merchant's instincts and a nobleman's ambitions. He knows 
that controlling the roads, bridges, and river ports can be more 
profitable than controlling the resources themselves. 
 
The Rangers of the Four Marquisates 
Each of the four eastern marquisates maintains a knightly order of mounted officers known as 
Rangers, established under the authority of their respective marquis following the Edict of the 
East. Unlike the traditional knightly orders of southern Cador, the Rangers are not primarily 
battlefield formations. They are frontier riders, scouts, bounty hunters, and enforcers who 
operate across vast territories where the reach of conventional government remains limited. 
Though Rangers frequently apprehend criminals, pursue outlaws, and assist local sheriffs, they 
are not impartial servants of the law. Their foremost duty is to carry out the will of their marquis. 
They deliver proclamations, enforce territorial claims, protect favored enterprises, investigate 
threats to their lord's interests, and undertake sensitive assignments that ordinary soldiers or 
magistrates cannot readily accomplish. A Ranger's authority derives from a commission bearing 
the marquis's seal, and the distinction between maintaining the peace and enforcing a 
nobleman's ambitions is not always clear.
